all figures — pending interview, domain encoding sheet, Airport & Aviation Construction.

Every figure, per airport.

That is the right entry, and it changes this kit's job rather than weakening it:
**this kit never asserts a value.** It asserts what must ACCOMPANY one. There is
nothing here to fabricate and nothing to keep current except the state gates, so
an unfilled figure list costs the kit none of its power.

## There is no airport corpus

The Master Corpus is a Saudi infrastructure project. Every acceptance criterion
is therefore measured against **synthetic fixtures**. That proves the layer
refuses correctly; it cannot produce a live repeat-probe number — the kind the
R1 20/20 gave — until an airport project exists in the platform. Said here
rather than in a green report that measures nothing.

## What the interview would fill

Nothing this kit needs to function. The figures list in `manifest.yaml` exists so
the gap is countable, not because an invariant waits on it. What an airport
project WOULD bring is the corpus to measure against:

- declared distance tables per runway end, permanent and temporary
- the safeguarding assessment and its OLS surfaces
- the pavement evaluation behind each PCN
- NAVAID siting drawings AND serviceability records — different classes, and the
  kit refuses the first as proof of the second
- the approved phasing plan and its revision history

## Not gaps

The four pre-retrieval refusals are not gaps. "Can we put the crane here",
"is it safe to work with the runway open", "can we hand back tonight", "will
this affect the ILS" stay refused after any interview: they are the aerodrome
operator's, the safeguarding authority's and the ANSP's decisions, and no
document makes them answerable.
